assets.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Create a new finished 16:9 landscape game environment background, natural live-action historical film still, not a 3D render. Input image 1 is ONLY the highest-priority spatial blockout: keep its eye-level camera, the low open-sided canvas REPORT SHELTER on the LEFT / middle, its worktable under the roof, and the unobstructed dirt road on the RIGHT leading north into the camp. Replace flat proxy materials with believable rough flax canvas, weathered timber, modest dark iron, coarse packed soil. Do not preserve the crude low-poly geometry, blank solid sky, or diagram-like color blocks.
This is a humble 6-metre-wide open dispatch shelter in a Three Kingdoms military camp at Wuzhang, not a command pavilion. Its whole front is OPEN between bare timber posts: clearly see the low wooden desk beneath the small sloping linen canopy. One modest local lantern at a post, some tied bamboo document rolls on the low desk, practical rope ties, sparse distant camp poles and ordinary low tents. There is NO central door, NO closed front curtain, NO grand axial entrance, NO monumental tent, NO paired ceremonial braziers. Main command tent stays OUT OF FRAME.
The shelter remains to the left and center, and right-side roadway has a clear walkable run away into depth, with restrained flag posts and wooden fence. Wide framing from normal standing eye height, no fisheye, no extreme angle. Bottom third is readable open rough ground for gameplay overlays.
Lighting: cool readable late dusk with soft grey sky and pale distant hills, retain detail in shadows, tiny localized amber from the single practical lantern, restrained dark teal/earth/aged linen colors. Do not turn this into pitch-black night or orange torch fantasy. Subtle fine film grain, real cloth weight and weave, imperfect wood; dry and damp soil patches with only tiny rough highlights, NO mirrored wet floor.
NO people anywhere, NO human silhouettes, NO text, no signs with writing, no UI, no letters, no labels, no watermarks, no gold ornament, no glowing borders. Deliver one polished natural photorealistic environment plate, exact 16:9 composition.

Use case: historical-scene. Create a new finished 16:9 landscape game environment background, natural live-action historical film still, not a 3D render. Keep the tent at approximately half the image width, roomy coarse earth foreground, a short practical timber fence on the left, partial ordinary supporting tents near the image edges. Replace the crude blockout with tactile real material; do not inherit flat planes or the solid sky.
This is Jiang Wei's own smaller 9m-wide by 10m-deep working tent, not the supreme command tent. Simple low sloping coarse grey-flax canvas roof, humble timber supports and rope lashings, no elevated terrace, no monumental roof or ceremonial portico. At its south-facing front center, one NARROW CLOSED dark grey canvas double flap reaches the ground; the two curtain halves meet shut. This is an EXTERIOR tent-front image: absolutely no view into the tent interior. A LOW modest wooden document table sits OUTSIDE on the RIGHT of its doorway, with two or three tied bamboo rolls, and ONE small hanging lantern close to that table. No paired braziers or symmetrical armies.
The main command tent is OUT OF FRAME to the left / northwest. The picture must read as a private working officer's modest closed tent, distinct from an OPEN dispatch canopy. Low fabric eaves, lived-in wrinkled linen, rough wood and muted iron; no gold.
Lighting: readable cool late dusk, soft grey-blue skylight, pale distant layered hills, shadows retain texture. Tiny local amber pool from the single lantern, restrained natural colors, subtle fine film grain, practical live-action materials. Dry and damp coarse packed earth, NO mirror puddles, no polished floor, no magical light. Bottom third has clear open ground for gameplay overlays.
NO people anywhere, NO silhouettes, NO text or writing, NO signboard, NO UI, NO labels, NO watermark, no grand command pavilion. Deliver one coherent natural photorealistic 16:9 environment plate.
